# PersonaMark

A persona's colour, drawn as a small diamond beside its name: the feature panel's persona visibility list marks each persona with it, and a tree row shows the personas it is visible to as a group of them (GAP-106).

- **Import:** `import { PersonaMark, PersonaMarkGroup } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Core
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; not linked to Figma yet.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/data-display-personamark--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { PersonaMark, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function PersonaMarkExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <PersonaMark color="#FF9800" />
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## PersonaMark

It forwards its ref to `HTMLSpanElement`. Its props are `PersonaMarkProps`, which extends `Omit<React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "color" | "children">`.

- `color`: `string`, **required**.

  The persona's colour, as the product holds it: any CSS colour, such as
  `"#FF9800"`. Drawn as given, in both themes.

- `name`: `string`, optional.

  The persona's name, for a mark that stands alone: it is then an image
  named by it. Leave it out when the name is shown beside the mark, as in a
  Checkbox's label: the mark is then hidden from assistive technology, so
  the name is not read twice.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## PersonaMarkGroup

The personas something is visible to, as a row of marks 2 apart: a tree
row's "Assigned personas". One image to assistive technology, named by
`label` and every persona's name. With no persona it draws nothing.

It forwards its ref to `HTMLSpanElement`. Its props are `PersonaMarkGroupProps`, which extends `Omit<React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children">`.

- `personas`: `readonly PersonaMarkPersona[]`, **required**.

  The personas, each drawn as its mark, in this order.

- `label`: `string`, optional, default `"Assigned personas"`.

  What the group is, read before the personas' names: "Assigned personas:
  Customer, Visitor". English by default; pass the product's own words.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Types these props take

### PersonaMarkPersona

From `@kozmos-ds/react`.

```ts
/** One persona in a group: its name and its colour. */
interface PersonaMarkPersona {
  name: string;
  color: string;
}
```
